title: The Hymn of Marrow Creek
premise: When Juniper Eastwick returns to Marrow Creek to bury her twin brother Jasper—whose body was found in the flooded quarry wearing her coat—she intends only to sign papers and leave. But the excavation crew breaking ground for the new reservoir unearths an iron door sealed from the inside, and the town's oldest families begin dying or vanishing, each corpse clutching something that belonged to the missing class of 1974. Juniper discovers she and Jasper were born as replacements: children offered to whatever waits behind the door, a bargain made by their grandfather to save the town during the drought of '74. The door has been holding a debt for fifty years, and it has chosen Juniper to settle it. To survive, she must return what was taken—including the truth about which twin actually died—and convince the town's surviving founders to give back the prosperity they bought with other people's children.
about_author: Ines Okafor is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing municipal records in small Appalachian towns before turning to fiction full-time. She writes horror rooted in civic secrets, family ledgers, and the things communities agree not to remember.

chapters.title: The Wrong Coat
chapters.summary: Juniper arrives in Marrow Creek for Jasper's funeral, unable to shake the detail no one will discuss: her brother drowned wearing her coat, her name stitched in the collar. POV alternates between Juniper and funeral director Dell Hargrove, who notices the body's hands are wrong. Emotional beat: grief laced with the first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Groundbreaking
chapters.summary: The reservoir crew hits iron forty feet down—an old cistern door, bolted shut from within. Juniper watches from the ridge as foreman Ray Odum touches the metal and immediately resigns, packing his truck without a word. POV: Juniper, with a brief interlude from Ray's departure. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Juniper cleans out Jasper's house and finds fifteen years of his journals documenting noises beneath the floorboards—scratching, humming, a hymn sung in two voices. His final entry reads: 'It stopped when you left. It never stopped for me.' POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt sharpening into terror.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: At the historical society, librarian Mabel Voss shows Juniper the 1974 drought ledger: seven families, seven entries, each recording a 'contribution' in exchange for water rights. The Eastwick entry lists two names—hers and Jasper's—with one crossed out. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the past stops being abstract.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper dives the quarry where Jasper was found and finds a second body preserved below—a girl from the class of '74, wearing Jasper's jacket. The swap went both directions, decades apart. POV: Juniper underwater, claustrophobic and close-third. Emotional beat: horror becoming personal betrayal.

chapters.title: Hymn in Two Voices
chapters.summary: Night. Juniper hears the hymn from Jasper's journals rising through her own floorboards, sung by a voice that is hers and isn't. She follows it to the excavation site, where the door has begun to sweat rust like old blood. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the supernatural becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: Seven Names
chapters.summary: Juniper tracks down the surviving founders. Six are dead or demented; only Ambrose Pell, ninety-one, still speaks plainly. He confirms the bargain: children given, water granted, and a renewal clause due 'when the last debt walks home.' POV: Ambrose's confession framed by Juniper's questions. Emotional beat: the banality of monstrous bargains.

chapters.title: The First Return
chapters.summary: Ray Odum, the resigned foreman, is found at the site having dug the door open three inches with his bare hands—dead, smiling, frostbitten in July. The town council votes to concrete over the pit. POV: rotating—councilwoman Ida Marsh, then Juniper. Emotional beat: institutional denial versus mounting evidence.

chapters.title: Concrete and Consequence
chapters.summary: The pour fails; the concrete sets around empty space, as if the pit refused filling. That night every clock in Marrow Creek stops at 3:14—the minute of the 1974 signing. POV: Ida Marsh, whose faith in the town begins to fracture. Emotional beat: power confronting its limits.

chapters.title: Jasper's Room
chapters.summary: Juniper finds a hidden room behind Jasper's closet wall: chalk sigils, photographs of herself asleep, and a list titled 'Ways In,' cataloguing how the thing below reaches people—dreams, mirrors, grief. He had been fighting it alone for years. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: love and horror entangled; her brother was a guardian, not a victim.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Face
chapters.summary: A stranger checks into the motel wearing Jasper's mannerisms, his laugh, his scar—but wrong, like a memory played at the wrong speed. Juniper confronts it; it speaks with her voice and asks her to 'come finish the verse.' POV: Juniper, with the entity's dialogue. Emotional beat: identity itself under siege.

chapters.title: Mabel's Confession
chapters.summary: Librarian Mabel Voss admits she was the eighth child in 1974—the one who ran, who let another take her place. The ledger's crossed-out name is hers. She gives Juniper the original contract and the ritual of return: everything taken must be given back willingly, by bloodline, before the equinox. POV: Mabel. Emotional beat: cowardice, guilt, and a late bid for redemption.

chapters.title: Ida's Price
chapters.summary: Councilwoman Ida Marsh tries to burn the ledger and destroy the evidence, protecting her family's water fortune. The fire turns on her; she survives but can no longer speak anything except the hymn. POV: Ida. Emotional beat: corruption consuming its host.

chapters.title: The Class of '74
chapters.summary: Juniper locates descendants of all seven contributed children. Some refuse to hear it; one, Theo Pell—Ambrose's grandson—already dreams the hymn and joins her. They map the debts: seven lives owed, six recoverable, one already spent. POV: Theo, an outsider's fresh terror. Emotional beat: alliance forming against impossible odds.

chapters.title: Descent Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Mabel teaches them the return rite at the sealed door: names spoken backward, debts laid on the threshold, blood to witness. During rehearsal the door answers—three knocks from inside, patient as a metronome. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dread braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: The town evacuates in panic as the aquifer reverses—water flowing uphill toward the pit. Ambrose Pell dies at sunset whispering 'it kept its half; we never kept ours.' Juniper realizes the entity isn't breaking the contract; the town is. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: moral inversion—the monster as creditor.

chapters.title: Which Twin
chapters.summary: At the graveside, Juniper finally admits the truth she's outrun for fifteen years: the drowned body wore her coat because it was meant for her, and Jasper took her place once already—as infants, in the crib, the night the humming started. Every sacrifice since has been his. POV: Juniper, raw interiority. Emotional beat: devastating self-knowledge.

chapters.title: Opening the Door
chapters.summary: Juniper, Theo, and Mabel descend to the door and perform the return. The bolts turn themselves. Inside: a dry cathedral of roots and standing water, and the seven taken children—aged, waiting, singing. The entity appears as both twins, whole. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: awe and horror fused; the climax begins.

chapters.title: The Verse Unfinished
chapters.summary: The entity demands completion: one twin above, one below, forever—the original terms. Juniper offers herself, but the Jasper-thing intervenes, revealing he has been bargaining from inside for fifteen years to buy her freedom. The hymn requires a willing voice; he volunteers. POV: alternating Juniper and Jasper. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax, loyalty outbidding death.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Jasper crosses fully; the remaining debts are paid as the founders' descendants surrender the water rights publicly, dissolving the covenant. The door seals—this time from the outside. The quarry floods clean. POV: Theo witnessing, Juniper shattered. Emotional beat: catharsis through loss.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Marrow Creek drinks honest water and buries its secrets in open record—Mabel publishes the ledger. Juniper stays, taking Jasper's house and his vigil, listening each night to floorboards gone silent. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: grief settling into guardianship.

chapters.title: The Hymn of Marrow Creek
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, Juniper hears the hymn once more—one voice now, hers, rising from the well she keeps capped but never fills. She sings the answering verse Jasper taught her in a dream, and the water goes still. Some debts become devotions. POV: Juniper, closing frame. Emotional beat: haunted peace; survival's price acknowledged, paid forward.
